cards.text: David's army just finished the war with the Ammonites. Some time later, another war breaks out at a place called Gezer. No rest for the warriors, friend. They're like my oven timer. The second one goes off, another one starts.

cards.question: A new war breaks out at Gezer. Who is Israel fighting this time?

cards.text: At Gezer, Sibbecai the Hushathite, one of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11:29), faces Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim. Sibbecai versus Sippai. Say THAT five times fast while somebody's swinging at you.

cards.question: At Gezer, Sibbecai the Hushathite kills Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim.
Sippai goes down at Gezer, and the Philistines are ___.

cards.text: Once again, there's a battle with the Philistines. This time, Elhanan son of Jair goes up against a man named Lahmi.

cards.question: Lahmi, the Philistine Elhanan faces, has a famous brother. Who is he?
In the battle with Lahmi, David himself is the one who strikes Lahmi down.

cards.text: Goliath. Yes, THAT Goliath, the Philistine David took down with a sling and a stone (1 Samuel 17:50). And now Elhanan son of Jair kills his brother Lahmi. Rough stretch for that family, friend.
The verse also mentions a spear with a shaft like a weaver's beam. Friend, that's not a spear. That's a fence post that got a job.
And there's ALSO a battle at Gath. There's a man there of great stature, and something about him is very unusual.

cards.question: What's unusual about the man of great stature at Gath?

answers.text: Six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot
A bronze coat of armor weighing five thousand shekels
An iron bed nine cubits long and four cubits wide

cards.question: The man at Gath has six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. Add them all up and that's ___ in all.

cards.text: TWENTY-FOUR! Friend, I pack cookie boxes with my MUSTACHE. This man could pack two boxes at once and still have fingers left over to wave. And the text says he too was descended from Rapha.
And this man doesn't stay quiet. He taunts Israel. Never a great plan.

cards.question: The man of great stature taunts Israel at Gath. Who kills him?

cards.text: And Shimei is David's brother. So that's David's own nephew stepping up. Talk about keeping it in the family.

cards.question: So these descendants of Rapha in Gath fall at the hands of ___ and his ___.

findings.problem: The opening card has 5 sentences: 'David's army just finished...', 'Some time later...', 'No rest for the warriors, friend.', 'They're like my oven timer.', 'The second one goes off, another one starts.' That is over the limit for the opening card.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card says David's army 'just finished the war with the Ammonites.' That fact comes from 1 Chronicles 20:1-3, which is outside the passage, and the card gives it no reference. The card cites only 1 Chronicles 20:4.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'Just finished' adds a closeness in time that the text doesn't give. Verse 4 says only 'Some time later', and the same card then says 'Some time later', so the two time markers pull against each other.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.
